drafts.after: Daniel sees thrones set in place. The Ancient of Days takes His seat. The court sits, and the books are opened. Jesus, Paul, and Revelation all put judgment in God's court before the final kingdom. Textual proof: Dan 7:9-10 shows a courtroom in heaven. Dan 7:22 says judgment was given to the saints of the Most High. The verdict comes first, and then the saints take the kingdom.
drafts.reason: V2: the three semicolon-joined clauses are now one idea per sentence, and the closing 'i.e.' legalese becomes a plain sentence. V3: 'issues a verdict' is now 'gives its verdict', 'is a heavenly judgment scene' becomes 'shows a courtroom in heaven', and 'a judicial verdict precedes their possession of the kingdom' becomes 'The verdict comes first, and then the saints take the kingdom'. Both citations (Dan 7:9-10, Dan 7:22), the phrase 'the saints of the Most High' and every claim (thrones set, the court sitting, the books opened, judgment placed in God's court before the final kingdom, the verdict before possession) are unchanged; no claim added or dropped.

drafts.after: An holy one answers: unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be made right. Hebrews shows the earthly sanctuary as a pattern of the heavenly sanctuary (Heb 8:1-2; 9:23-24). Leviticus 16 describes how the sanctuary was cleansed with blood each year. Textual proof: Daniel's time prophecy ends at a sanctuary event. Hebrews puts Christ's ministry in the true tabernacle. Leviticus defines what "cleansed/right" means in the priestly setting — the sin that piled up is taken out of the sanctuary.
drafts.reason: V2: the five-clause 'Textual proof' chain is split into one idea per sentence. V3: 'locates ... in the true tabernacle' becomes 'puts', 'priestly context' becomes 'the priestly setting', 'annual cleansing' becomes 'how the sanctuary was cleansed with blood each year', and 'removal of accumulated sin' becomes 'the sin that piled up is taken out'. The 2,300 wording 'unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be made right' is byte-identical, as are Heb 8:1-2; 9:23-24, Leviticus 16 and the quoted "cleansed/right".

drafts.after: The little power speaks against the Most High. It wears out the saints, and it rules for a time, times, and a dividing of time. First principle: that time has a limit. The wearing out of the saints comes to an end.

V3: 'holds sway' becomes 'rules', and 'prophetic time is bounded — the wear-out has a stopwatch on it' is said in everyday words. The KJV time phrase 'a time, times, and a dividing of time', the Most High, the saints and the label First principle: are byte-identical (I1).

drafts.after: The judgment came, and the saints of the Most High possessed the kingdom. Textual proof: the heavenly court in v9-10 gives its verdict, and then the saints receive dominion. Paul writes that the saints will judge the world and even angels (1 Cor 6:2-3). Revelation 20:4 shows thrones set up and judgment handed to those who reign with Christ.
drafts.reason: V2: the missing article and the verbless clause are fixed, so 'heavenly court (v9-10) issues a verdict' now reads as plain subject-verb-object, and 'shall judge' becomes 'will judge'. V3: 'thrones and judgment given to those who reign with Christ' becomes 'thrones set up and judgment handed to those who reign with Christ'. v9-10, 1 Cor 6:2-3 and Revelation 20:4 are byte-identical, and every claim (the verdict, then dominion, the saints judging world and angels, thrones and judgment with Christ) stands.

drafts.after: Dominion under the whole heaven passes to the saints of the Most High. It is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions serve Him. First principle: the story does not end with the beast's empire. It ends with the saints' inheritance under the Son of man.
